_why: The LINEPIN else-arm was reached in two cases -- `prov is None` (genuinely unjudgeable) and `prov` present with `_changed_since` False (checked, clean) -- and printed the same cannot-judge sentence for both, while a PINDRIFT finding on the next line of the SAME output named that very sha. The arm destroyed exactly the distinction its own comment exists to preserve. Both directions are mutated: collapsing the arms back, and relabelling the honest case as checked.

mutations.name: the-arms-are-collapsed-again
mutations._mechanism: The defect. A pin verified against a real provenance sha is reported as having none, in an output that names that sha three lines earlier.

mutations.name: the-honest-case-is-relabelled-as-checked
mutations._mechanism: The opposite error, and the tempting one: making every LINEPIN claim it was checked. A pin with NO provenance sha would then assert it was measured against one, which is the same lie pointing the other way -- and strictly worse, because it manufactures confidence instead of withholding it.
mutations.find: ("LINEPIN", lineno, f"`{rel}:{tail}` — line pin with no provenance commit to check it against")
mutations.replace: ("LINEPIN", lineno, f"`{rel}:{tail}` — line pin; `{rel}` unchanged since the document's provenance")
